From 73b5ab27ab2ee616f2709dc212c2b0007894a12e Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Hsiao Chien Sung <shawn.sung@mediatek.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Dec 2023 13:58:46 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/mediatek: Fix underrun in VDO1 when switches off the
 layer

Do not reset Merge while using CMDQ because reset API doesn't
wait for frame done event as CMDQ does and could lead to
underrun when the layer is switching off.

Fixes: aaf94f7c3ae6 ("drm/mediatek: Add display merge async reset control")

Reviewed-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.com>
Reviewed-by: AngeloGioacchino Del Regno <angelogioacchino.delregno@collabora.com>
Signed-off-by: Hsiao Chien Sung <shawn.sung@mediatek.com>
Link: https://patchwork.kernel.org/project/dri-devel/patch/20231214055847.4936-23-shawn.sung@mediatek.com/
Signed-off-by: Chun-Kuang Hu <chunkuang.hu@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_merge.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_merge.c
index e525a6b9e5b0..22f768d923d5 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_merge.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_merge.c
@@ -103,7 +103,7 @@ void mtk_merge_stop_cmdq(struct device *dev, struct cmdq_pkt *cmdq_pkt)
 	mtk_ddp_write(cmdq_pkt, 0, &priv->cmdq_reg, priv->regs,
 		      DISP_REG_MERGE_CTRL);
 
-	if (priv->async_clk)
+	if (!cmdq_pkt && priv->async_clk)
 		reset_control_reset(priv->reset_ctl);
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/gpu/drm/mediatek/mtk_disp_merge.c`**
   - The condition for resetting the `priv->reset_ctl` has been modified. 
   - The original line:
     ```c
     if (priv->async_clk)
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     if (!cmdq_pkt && priv->async_clk)
     ```
   - This change ensures that the reset control is only invoked when `cmdq_pkt` is not present, preventing potential underrun issues when switching off the layer.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in the `mtk_disp_merge.c` file addresses a specific bug related to the handling of the reset control during the layer shutdown process. By adding the condition to check for `cmdq_pkt`, the patch prevents the reset API from being called prematurely, which could lead to underrun issues. This change is directly related to the previously introduced feature of display merge async reset control, as indicated by the fix reference in the patch description. The patch effectively enhances the stability of the display merging process by ensuring that the reset only occurs under appropriate conditions.

Here is the commit message:
drm/mediatek: Fix underrun in VDO1 when switches off the
 layer

Do not reset Merge while using CMDQ because reset API doesn't
wait for frame done event as CMDQ does and could lead to
underrun when the layer is switching off.

Fixes: aaf94f7c3ae6 ("drm/mediatek: Add display merge async reset control")

Reviewed-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.com>
Reviewed-by: AngeloGioacchino Del Regno <angelogioacchino.delregno@collabora.com>
Signed-off-by: Hsiao Chien Sung <shawn.sung@mediatek.com>
Link: https://patchwork.kernel.org/project/dri-devel/patch/20231214055847.4936-23-shawn.sung@mediatek.com/
Signed-off-by: Chun-Kuang Hu <chunkuang.hu@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug is caused by the reset API being called without waiting for the frame done event when using CMDQ, which can lead to an underrun condition when the layer is being switched off. This occurs because the reset is executed regardless of whether a command queue packet (`cmdq_pkt`) is present, potentially disrupting the ongoing operations and causing data loss.

Here is the patch:
 
 void mtk_merge_stop_cmdq(struct device *dev, struct cmdq_pkt *cmdq_pkt)
 {
 	struct mtk_disp_merge *priv = dev_get_drvdata(dev);
 
 	if (priv->mute_support)
 		mtk_ddp_write(cmdq_pkt, 0x1, &priv->cmdq_reg, priv->regs,
 			      DISP_REG_MERGE_MUTE_0);
 
 	mtk_ddp_write(cmdq_pkt, 0, &priv->cmdq_reg, priv->regs,
 		      DISP_REG_MERGE_CTRL);
 
-	if (priv->async_clk)
+	if (!cmdq_pkt && priv->async_clk)
 		reset_control_reset(priv->reset_ctl);
 }



```c

```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the reset API (`reset_control_reset`) is called without ensuring that the command queue packet (`cmdq_pkt`) is present. This can disrupt ongoing operations when the layer is being switched off, leading to an underrun condition. The check for `priv->async_clk` does not prevent the reset from being executed if `cmdq_pkt` is NULL, which can cause data loss.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!cmdq_pkt && priv->async_clk)
```
```c
reset_control_reset(priv->reset_ctl);
```
Reason:
The fix modifies the condition to ensure that the reset is only called when there is no command queue packet (`cmdq_pkt`) and `priv->async_clk` is true. This prevents the reset from being executed prematurely, allowing the system to wait for the frame done event, thus avoiding the underrun condition when the layer is switched off.
